description: Block-by-block trace of a vLLM-V1-style paged KV allocator: allocation, prefix sharing by reference count, freeing to the free queue, cache revival, tenant isolation by cache_salt, and LRU eviction. Video sequence 3 (KV paging); R-XIII.2, R-XIII.3, R-XIII.5.

labels.hashes: illustrative digests (same chain structure as vLLM, different serialization)
labels.hash_serialization: SHA-256 over: parent digest (32 bytes) | number of tokens (uint32 big-endian) | token IDs (uint32 big-endian each) | extra keys as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces)
labels.classes: mechanism class A (vLLM V1); pool size, request lengths and tenants are class C reference choices for the animation

D.reason: cache_salt is an extra key of block 0; every later hash chains block 0

E.rule: E needs every free block from the queue head up to and including block 2 of the shared SYSTEM+TOOLS chain (chosen to create memory pressure)

F.why: the chain's tail block was evicted first, so blocks 0-1 of the chain still hit

simplifications: One KV-cache group (full attention only); one engine step computes a whole prompt (no chunked prefill).
No preemption: request sizes are chosen so running requests never run out of blocks.
Background requests share no prefixes; each has its own cache_salt.
When several unhashed blocks are freed together they are prepended so that the request's last block ends at the head; vLLM's exact order inside one prepend batch is not documented in our notes.
Request E's prompt length is computed from the free queue at its arrival (rule in summary.E.rule).
Output token IDs are synthetic; block hashes of decode blocks include them.
